title: ACID Properties & Transaction Isolation Levels
source: IBM Db2 & Cloudant Distributed Data Systems
content: Relational transactions guarantee ACID properties: Atomicity (all-or-nothing completion), Consistency (transitions maintain database invariants), Isolation (concurrent transactions execute without interference), and Durability (committed changes persist across crashes). ANSI SQL defines four isolation levels: Read Uncommitted (dirty reads possible), Read Committed (prevents dirty reads, non-repeatable reads possible), Repeatable Read (prevents non-repeatable reads, phantom reads possible), and Serializable (strict serial execution).
key_takeaways: Higher isolation levels increase locking overhead and deadlocks

title: Database Indexing: B-Trees vs Hash Indexes & SQL Optimization
source: IBM Query Optimization & Data Engineering Manual
content: Indexes dramatically accelerate query retrieval at the expense of insert/update latency. B-Tree / B+Tree indexes keep keys sorted in self-balancing balanced tree nodes, supporting both equality and range scans (e.g. BETWEEN, >, <). Hash indexes offer O(1) equality lookups but cannot perform range scans. SQL optimization techniques: use EXPLAIN to inspect query execution plans, avoid SELECT *, ensure indexed columns are not wrapped in functions, and normalize up to 3NF to eliminate redundancy.
key_takeaways: B+ Trees store records in leaves for fast sequential traversal
Hash indexes only support point equality queries
Composite index column order must match query filter prefixes
